text:
maya: Hey team — opening thread for APAC account setup. We need Elastic IP / ENI / VPC quota increases in ap-northeast-1 for an upcoming Dedicated GPU pool.

Irene: Can you list exact numbers you want bumped?

maya: Estimating 450 Elastic IPs (public IPs for node-level NAT and some legacy per-node EIP usage). ENIs: want 200 per subnet across 3 subnets (we hit ENI exhaustion when pods scale). VPC limit: default 5 VPCs -> request 20. Also want IPv6 enablement to reduce IPv4 pressure.

Tony: Curious — can we avoid that many EIPs by switching to NLB static IP targets or using IPv6 dual-stack?

maya: NLB helps but we still need some EIPs for management plane + older customer configs. IPv6 would reduce new IPv4 needs but customer networks still require IPv4 for now.

Samir: Filed an AWS support case: 1234567891. AWS asked for a capacity plan + justification and the specific service quota codes. Putting AWS CLI request example here for tracking: 

Samir: ```
aws service-quotas request-service-quota --service-code ec2 --quota-code L-0263 --desired-value 450 --region ap-northeast-1
```

maya: Also submitted a separate request for ENI per subnet. AWS support wants projected node counts and VPC CIDR details. They flagged that per-account ENI limits are enforced per AZ.

Irene: Quick cost note — attached EIPs have a small monthly cost (and unattached ones are expensive). At 450 EIPs the ballpark monthly cost is ~1.6k USD just for EIP charges if all are attached. We should compare with NLB static IP + IPv6 options.

Tony: Ops question — are any of these GPU nodes going to have public IPs by design? If we can NAT at the subnet level we cut EIP count significantly.

maya: For latency-sensitive inference endpoints we sometimes attach public IP to node to avoid NAT hop. We need to document which pools require public IP and which can sit behind NLB.

Samir: AWS replied to the case: they need (1) monthly projected instance counts for next 12 months, (2) VPC CIDR & AZ mapping, (3) justification for per-subnet ENIs, and (4) confirmation whether IPv6 will be enabled. They also provided a reference quota code list to use.

maya: I'll draft the projection table: month1 50 nodes, month3 200, month6 400, month12 600 (mostly g5/g5n/g5a workloads). Requesting the EIP and ENI increases now to avoid throttling during ramp.

Irene: Can you also include a note about autoscaling behavior and prefix delegation? If we can use shared NAT gateways with source IP preservation it's worth exploring.

Samir: Action items: (1) Maya: upload capacity plan + VPC CIDR map to case 1234567891, (2) Irene: run cost comparison EIP vs NLB+IPv6 by EOM, (3) Tony: audit pools that require node public IPs. I'll update the case once docs attached.

aws-support-bot: Support case 1234567891 updated — request queued for internal review.

maya: Tagging @Samir @Irene @Tony — I'll update here when the case number moves to resolution. :thumbsup:
